notes:
☠️ THIS FILE IS THE STRIP, AND UNTIL 2026-09-06 IT WAS NOT. The delivery beat in home-beats.json carried its OWN copy of these tiles and InstallsPanel read that copy, so this manifest was imported by nothing: editing it changed no pixel, and the studio's Installs strip editor was a control wired to nothing. Both now read here. If you add a beat that shows a strip, hand it a manifest, do not paste the list into the beat.
Every installation and delivery article's PHOTOGRAPHS, one or two frames each. THE FIRST TILE IS FIXED: it is the frame the beat led with and Jarich asked to keep it at the start. Places only, never names.
☠️ PHOTOGRAPHS ONLY. Nine tiles were removed because they were advertising, not evidence: the five p### files are designed cards (two proof of delivery panels with a QR code and an ORDER NOW button, two monthly price cards, one thank you card), the two install-2026 files are marketing collateral (a studio render still captioned Step 4, and a How We Install promo graphic), one v frame is overprinted with a Bound to Pangasinan title, and one is a screenshot of a map. The naming holds the rule: p### means a poster the design desk made, v### means a frame from real footage. Anything added later that carries overlaid selling text, a price, a render or a screenshot does not belong on this strip.
☠️ A PRICE IN THE FRAME IS A PRICE, WHOEVER PAINTED IT (Jarich, 2026-09-06). v020-1 was a real photograph of a real install and it still went, because the clinic's own banner behind the crew read GET YOUR DREAM DENTAL BRACES AT 40 PERCENT OFF, LOWEST DOWN PAYMENT, under their illuminated name. The rule is not about who made the artwork, it is about what a visitor reads on our home page. The same install is still on the strip through v020-2, which is the crew and the unit with no signage in shot. All 30 remaining tiles were checked for prices and offers; this was the only one.
EXTENDABLE: the strip reads any number of entries and re-times itself.
☠️ FIVE FRAMES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK AT TILE SIZE (ruled 2026-09-06). v033-8, v039-1, v039-2, v039-5 and v301-2 are 360 pixels wide at source with no larger copy anywhere. A tile on this strip is 288x216 css, and cover at a floor of 1.75 needs 504 across, so a 360 wide source scores min(360/288, 640/216) = 1.25 and sits visibly soft beside everything around it. ☠️ This paragraph previously quoted 384 css and 768 device px, which are action-reels' numbers: one reason string was written once and pasted into both files. A note that describes a different list's geometry is worse than none, because it reads as measured. They are documentary article photographs whose captions describe the exact frame, so they are never swapped for a lookalike and never upscaled. They keep their place IN the articles, where they render small; they only leave the large strips. The same five are listed in the machine readable `stripUnsafe` map on this file, keyed by filename, so a picker or a future builder can refuse them without parsing this paragraph. ☠️ NEITHER OF THESE TWO MANIFESTS IS GENERATED BY A SCRIPT: unlike crew-shots and training-media there is no builder to enforce the refusal, so the only guard is this key and whoever reads it.
☠️ tilePx IS THE DECISION NOW; THE stripUnsafe MAP BELOW IS DOCUMENTATION. tilePx is the largest CSS width a tile in this strip renders at, MEASURED on a production build at 1440 and at 390, not remembered: 288x216 css on a desktop (270x202 on a 390 phone). A file is too soft here when it cannot supply the floor across that tile. The tiles are 4:3 with object-fit: cover, so the image is scaled by max(tileW/w, tileH/h) and a file passes when min(w/288, h/216) >= 1.75, which is 504 across. The floor is 1.75, not 2: it moved on 2026-09-06 so 720 wide material clears a 384 tile. For the portrait photographs on this strip the width is the axis that binds, but the test is both axes and the source's long side is never the thing to compare.
 tileHeightPx makes the test exact cover rather than width alone: the tile is 288x216 css on a desktop and 270x203 on a phone. A file passes when min(srcW/288, srcH/216) >= 1.75, which is 504 across and 378 down. This strip carries no video, so its video tile is null rather than absent.
☠️ THE VIDEO TILE IS null, NOT ABSENT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. null means MEASURED AND EMPTY: this strip takes images only, so every clip is refused and the studio says so in the list's own words. An ABSENT key would mean nobody has measured it, which the studio labels 'video tile not declared' and treats as barring nothing. Both states look identical from the outside and mean opposite things, which is the same proxy trap this file already carries a note about: absence cannot distinguish 'not applicable' from 'not checked'. InstallsPanel renders StripTile, which emits an Image and has no video branch at all, so null is a fact about the component and not a preference.
 tileFit is 'cover', measured as the computed object-fit on the rendered tile, not read off the stylesheet. ☠️ THE OPERATOR IS min, NOT max, AND THIS NOTE HAD IT BACKWARDS. The SCALE to cover is max(tileW/w, tileH/h); the RESOLUTION RATIO is its reciprocal, min(w/tileW, h/tileH), and that is the form implementations use. A cover tile crops to fill, so the axis that fills first must supply the pixels and the SMALLER ratio decides. contain is max of the ratios, which parts.json takes. A 'contain' tile would letterbox instead and need less, which is why the parts rows are a different case and not merely a smaller one.
